_doc: Shrink-only ratchet for the canonical radon_raw_nloc block band (1031.9, p95, corpus revision 1). Cutover 2026-08-01, seeded at the modules already over the band when module-sloc-cap-radon was repointed off its own invented <=1000 cap onto the one canonical threshold table (.gzkit/rules/complexity-thresholds.md § Invariant). NEVER add an entry to silence a fresh violation — that is the laundering ADR-0.0.73 Boundary Invariant #8 forbids. `ceiling` is the value the gate enforces: the ceiling a module may never exceed again, driven down to current SLOC so no headroom is silently re-consumable (GHI #853). `sloc_at_cutover` is the dated 2026-08-01 measurement, preserved as a historical record and never read by the gate. A module that drops under the band must surrender its entry entirely, and a module that shrinks while still over the band must surrender the difference — which is what makes the list shrink-only. An operator may raise a ceiling deliberately (see fc3f0956); the raise then surfaces as slack the next time the module shrinks, recorded-and-visible rather than blocked. Enforced by .gzkit/chores/module-sloc-cap-radon/check_module_size.py.
ceilings_tightened: 2026-08-22 (GHI #853): 928 SLOC of unrecorded slack surrendered across four entries. 2026-08-26 (GHI #885): operator override raised validate_cmd 1242->1251 and parser_maintenance 1514->1521 to seat the corpus_retirement_witness scope. A new validator scope structurally requires lines in both modules (the registry lives in one, the flag in the other), so the alternative was unrelated refactoring of two 1200+ SLOC modules on a defect fix. Surfaces as slack the next time either shrinks. 2026-08-26: LIST EMPTIED. The block band moved from p95 (1031.9) to p99 (3143.82) on operator amendment, and every remaining entry was under the new band, so all five surrendered per the shrink-only rule. The 2026-08-26 raises recorded above are therefore moot -- they were made against the p95 band hours before it was retired.
